Keeping peptides cool in Phoenix

Phoenix weather records began downtown in 1896 and moved to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport in the 1950s.6 At the airport station, about 1,107 feet above sea level, the 1991 to 2020 normals put the July high at 106.5 °F and the July low at 84.5 °F.3 An average year has 111.3 days at or above 100 °F, 173.4 days at or above 90 °F and just 0.6 nights at or below freezing.1 The first 100 °F day usually arrives around May 2 and the last around October 5.2

Recent years have run hotter than those averages. The National Weather Service ranks 2024 as the warmest year in Phoenix records and 2025 as the second warmest.76 In 2024 Phoenix stayed at or above 100 °F for a record 113 days in a row, from May 27 to September 16, and reached 110 °F or more on a record 70 days.2 The all-time high is 122 °F, set on June 26, 1990.2

Heat is not spread evenly across the Valley. These are the NOAA stations behind this page and seven other Maricopa County city pages, with their 1991 to 2020 normals:

Tempe ASU Tempe, Chandler 105.9 °F12 75.8 °F12 106.813

Sky Harbor has the warmest July nights in the table, 1.9 to 8.7 °F warmer than the other six stations, while Youngtown in the West Valley logs the most 100 °F days.

Peptide makers publish general storage rules rather than heat limits. Bachem says its products are typically shipped at ambient temperature, with the recommended long-term storage condition noted on the label.4 Its general rule is a refrigerator (4 °C) for short-term use and a freezer below -15 °C, in a tightly closed container, for anything kept longer.4 How much heat a particular research peptide can take has not been published, so the storage condition on the label or product page is the one to follow.420 In a Phoenix summer that means taking a delivered box indoors right away, never leaving it on a porch or in a parked car, and storing each vial as its label or product page directs. The storage guide goes into more detail.

About Phoenix

Phoenix is the seat of Maricopa County and the capital of Arizona.21 The Census Bureau estimates 1,665,481 residents on July 1, 2025, up from an April 2020 estimates base of 1,608,349, on 518.5 square miles of land.2223 The city calls itself the fifth largest in the United States.24 For planning it is split into 15 urban villages, each with a committee appointed by the mayor and council, among them Ahwatukee Foothills, Camelback East, Encanto, Laveen, Maryvale and South Mountain.5 The city counts 41,000 acres of desert parks and mountain preserves and more than 200 miles of trails.24 South Mountain Park/Preserve alone covers more than 16,000 acres across three ranges, and Dobbins Lookout, at 2,330 feet, is its highest point open to the public.25

Downtown holds the Phoenix Bioscience Core, a 30-acre innovation district created in 2004 as a joint initiative of the City of Phoenix, the Arizona Board of Regents, Arizona State University and the University of Arizona.2627 Institutions in or next to the district include TGen (the Translational Genomics Research Institute), the University of Arizona College of Medicine-Phoenix, two ASU health colleges, Northern Arizona University allied health programs and the NIH's National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases.26 The medical school opened its four-year MD program in 2007, in former Phoenix Union High School buildings.28 ASU's new John Shufeldt School of Medicine and Medical Engineering welcomes its first class of students in the 2026 to 2027 school year.27 Mayo Clinic's Phoenix location includes Mayo Clinic Hospital and a cancer center with a proton beam therapy facility.29 Sky Harbor, which the city bought in 1935, served more than 51.6 million passengers in 2025.30

Nearby

Phoenix is the hub of our Maricopa County pages, which run north to south from Anthem, along Interstate 17,31 to Queen Creek in the southeast Valley.23 Measured in a straight line from the Sky Harbor weather station, Tempe is about 5 miles southeast, Glendale about 13 miles northwest, Mesa about 17 miles east, Gilbert about 17 miles east-southeast and Scottsdale about 19.5 miles north-northeast.233 Chandler lies in the southeast part of greater Phoenix.32 Pages for Fountain Hills, Peoria, Buckeye and Surprise complete our county pages. The other two areas we cover start at Las Vegas and Riverside, and the locations page lists every place.

Frequently asked questions

Do you ship research peptides to Phoenix?

Yes. Phoenix orders ship from the USA and Canada under the same policy as every order across the United States, and addresses elsewhere in Maricopa County are handled the same way. Each product page lists its strengths and stock status before checkout. The shipping page explains how orders are sent, and the returns page covers a parcel that arrives damaged or incomplete.

Is there a D2C Peptides location in Phoenix?

No. D2C Peptides lists no address in Phoenix or anywhere else in Maricopa County, which is why this page carries no street address, phone number or map. Phoenix customers are served by shipping only, under the shipping policy. Questions about an order go through the contact page.

When is a Phoenix delivery most exposed to heat?

From early May to early October. In an average year Phoenix reaches its first 100 °F day around May 2 and its last around October 5,2 and the normal July low at Sky Harbor is 84.5 °F, so a box left outside overnight gets little relief.3 Bachem, a peptide maker, says freeze-dried peptides may be shipped at room temperature but should be kept below -15 °C for longer storage,4 so bring the box indoors promptly and store each vial as its label or product page directs.

Are these products sold for personal use?

No. Every product is sold for laboratory research only, and each product page carries the notice "For research use only. Not for human or veterinary use.". Who may order, and on what terms, is covered by the research use policy. The medical disclaimer describes what the information on these pages is and is not meant for. A question about treatment or dosing for a person belongs with a licensed clinician.
